key_insight: A per-page write timestamp plus a regenerate trap turns expiry into a page fault, so data with an authoritative copy elsewhere needs no refresh.
killer_doubt: Cs is sized by the Cs/Cbl sense ratio, so 10 ms retention saves ~1.2-1.5x Cs, not 3x. KV and cold pages idle >10 ms would regenerate constantly.
decisive_experiment: Trace study (~$30k): log page reuse intervals for LLM serving and training on GPU hosts, then count bytes idle >10 ms and the regeneration traffic. Pair it with a sense-margin simulation of Cs versus retention.
prior_art: RANA (ISCA 2018) and ZEM refresh skipping; Flikker; HRM clean-page refetch (DSN 2014); in-study I-10659, I-00496 (DROP), I-03014 (HOLD).

key_insight: Retired DRAM dies show little wear-out, so retest and rebinning recover wafer-free bits. Die-level reclaim could restack them into denser CXL packages.
killer_doubt: Decap plus re-bump costs more than reballing whole packages, which GreenSKU and Structera X already reuse. Decap fallout is likely 10-30% (estimate), and the DDR4 pool is one-time.
decisive_experiment: Decap 200 retired DDR4 FBGA packages chemically and by laser, re-bond the dies on a test substrate, and compare yield, retention tail and cost per GB with reballed whole packages. Under $150k.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X; ITAD resale; failure-analysis decap; in-study I-04852, I-05321, I-06172 (all DROP).

key_insight: Strain-driven rolling multiplies area per footprint by about the number of turns. That is a real volumetric density trick, useful only where footprint is the scarce axis.
killer_doubt: Rolling folds already-lithographed area: 20 turns need ~20x the patterned area, so litho cost per bit stays planar. Edge-contacting 20 turns at ~40 nm pitch is unsolved.
decisive_experiment: A spreadsheet of patterned area, wafers per GB and roll yield settles cost per bit. Only if footprint matters, roll a 5-turn IGZO TFT membrane (~$100k) and measure turn-to-turn registration.
prior_art: Rolled-up nanotechnology (O. G. Schmidt, IFW Dresden; X. Li, UIUC): rolled capacitors and TFTs; in-study I-00027, I-10175 (both DROP).

key_insight: Learning-cycle cost, not physics, gates new memory cells. Split lots across idle U.S. tools could cut a cell team's first-silicon spend by maybe 5-10x.
killer_doubt: NNCI and Natcast/NSTC already sell tool time. Cross-site contamination rules (Cu, Au, Hf, In) and metrology drift block split lots; integration skill, not tool hours, is scarce.
decisive_experiment: Broker one 3-site split lot of an IGZO 2T0C test wafer (ALD, etch, test) through NNCI sites. Measure turnaround, cost, contamination refusals and cross-site variation against a single-site run. ~$150k.
prior_art: NSF NNCI user facilities; CHIPS NSTC/Natcast prototyping (Albany); NY CREATES; Science Exchange lab marketplace; MOSIS shuttles [training knowledge].

key_insight: Matrix's ~4-masks-per-deck poly-diode stacking, with a capacitor replacing the antifuse, gives transistor-free DUV decks with unlimited write endurance.
killer_doubt: A 4F2 planar MIM at F=40 nm holds ~0.2 fF. Poly-Si junction leakage (~10-100 fA at 85 C, estimate) gives ~0.2-2 ms retention: 30-300x more refresh than 64 ms.
decisive_experiment: University fab, ~$150k: build 2-deck poly-Si punch-through selectors on 0.2 fF MIM caps. Measure hold leakage at 25-85 C, V/2 disturb across 1k half-selected cells, and retention distributions.
prior_art: Matrix Semiconductor/SanDisk 3D OTP; Phase B N-85 crested-barrier 1S1C (the better selector route); in-study I-08759, I-04677 (both DROP).

key_insight: A 10-20 K wafer-to-gas gap drives sub-micron particles away at ~0.2 mm/s, faster than diffusion deposition, so particle protection can travel with the wafer instead of the building.
killer_doubt: FOUP/EFEM mini-environments already isolate wafers, so the ballroom sets little yield. Cleanroom systems are ~5-10% of fab capex (estimate), so ISO 5 to ISO 7 saves ~2-4%.
decisive_experiment: Expose heated (+15 K) and ambient bare wafers in ISO 5 and ISO 7 air inside a FOUP-like enclosure for 24 h, then count added particles >20 nm on a wafer inspector. Under $100k.
prior_art: Stratmann/Fissan heated-wafer thermophoretic suppression (late 1980s); Sandia/Intel thermophoretic EUV-mask protection; FOUP/SMIF mini-environment fabs [training knowledge].

key_insight: Decoding inside each tier makes line-end contacts scale as log2(N), not N. Active local drivers hold unselected lines at a rail, unlike passive Vt-coded series selects.
killer_doubt: Identical tiers decode identically: unique addresses need per-tier masks, deposition-coded Vt or programming. IGZO drivers at ~10-30 cm2/Vs may make line ends ~3-10x larger.
decisive_experiment: University fab, ~$250k: a 4-tier IGZO stack with deposition-coded Vt per tier plus same-film NMOS decoders. Measure address margin, Vt spread against 100-200 mV coding steps, and wordline rise time at 3 V.
prior_art: SanDisk US9240420 in-tier oxide-TFT word line select (via search snippet); US9418743 3D NAND local WL drivers; Macronix layer select; in-study N-47, I-11544.

key_insight: Stamps place thousands of thin DRAM tiles per cycle over compute, avoiding die-to-wafer bonder throughput, with old-fab tiles at ~0.1-0.3 pJ/bit.
killer_doubt: Commodity DRAM wafers lack a release layer. Print placement is ~+/-1.5 um, forcing >=5-10 um via pitch, while SoIC/SeDRAM hybrid bonding already runs <=9 um in production.
decisive_experiment: Thin 20 old-node DRAM dies to ~10 um on release tape and print them onto a heater-equipped logic test wafer with adaptive-patterned vias. Measure placement error, via yield, pJ/bit and 85-95 C retention. ~$300k.
prior_art: X-Celeprint/Rogers micro-transfer printing; Deca adaptive patterning; SeDRAM (IEDM 2020) and TSMC SoIC hybrid bonding; in-study I-02653 (DROP).

key_insight: Reusing a 300-layer NAND stack as two-phase CCD strings adds multilevel packets to the no-per-bit-device CCD idea, and an IGZO channel holds packets for seconds.
killer_doubt: Up to ~300 transfers per read: at imec's >98% CTE ~0.2% survives, and 4-level packets need ~3x tighter loss. 150 ns implies ~1-2 GHz clocks versus 4-6 MHz shown.
decisive_experiment: Superseded by the I-08879/I-10793 CTE-versus-clock test chip. Revisit only if per-transfer CTE >=0.99999 at >=500 MHz; then measure 4-level packet error rates on a 64-gate string.
prior_art: imec IGZO CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024 planar; IMW 2026 vertical, word lines as phase gates); 1970s Intel/Fairchild CCD; in-study I-10793, I-08879.

key_insight: Tying every fourth tier to one clock phase deletes the staircase: four phase contacts serve ~200 tiers from one hole mask, and recirculation doubles as refresh.
killer_doubt: The far packet needs ~200 transfers: at CTE 0.98 ~2% survives (>=0.99995 needed). 50 ns average implies ~2 GHz against imec's 4-6 MHz; whole blocks shift per access.
decisive_experiment: Fold into the I-08879 test chip (~$250k): add an 8-16-tier phase-tied vertical coupon through a NAND-pilot partner. Measure plane RC, shift energy per bit and per-transfer CTE from 10 MHz to 1 GHz at 85 C.
prior_art: imec 3D IGZO CCD (IMW 2026, word lines as phase gates); Intel 2416/Fairchild F464 recirculating CCDs; in-study I-02002 (same phase-tying), I-10793.

key_insight: Closed-flux circumferential NiFe rings read non-destructively and write magnetically, so there is no charge-fluence wall; one hole mask with aqueous etch and plating builds the array.
killer_doubt: A 5 x 50 nm NiFe ring links ~2.5e-16 Wb; a 10% tilt in 1 ns induces ~25 nV. A 10 Oe word-plane field needs ~1.6 A per mm width.
decisive_experiment: None warranted at memory scale. If pursued, plate NiFe in 200 nm MacEtch holes through two doped-Si planes (~$80k) and measure inductive read signal and half-select disturb versus diameter.
prior_art: UNIVAC/Bell plated-wire memory (1960s); IBM racetrack; Phase B N-82 racetrack-in-hole; in-study I-08865, I-04287 (both DROP on signal).

key_insight: Frozen weights need zero write endurance. A generic crossbar base wafer customised only in via layers turns each model into a ROM chiplet with no per-model mask set.
killer_doubt: Taalas HC1 already hardwires weights in N6 metal/via ROM. Multibeam e-beam writes one mask's area in ~10 h, so 8 via levels per 300 mm wafer take ~200-400 tool-hours.
decisive_experiment: Cost model (~$20k): multibeam write time per via level per wafer versus a ~$100k DUV via mask amortised over chips per model version, plus selector-less via-crosspoint sneak-path read margin.
prior_art: Taalas HC1 mask-ROM weights, AMD acquiring (prior logs); Matrix 3D OTP; eASIC via-configurable ASICs; in-study I-02068 (same mechanism, DROP), I-02186 (ADVANCE).
